inputs.question: What does the Bible say about worry?

answer: Two of the retrieved passages speak directly to worry. Jesus says, “don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient” [S1]. First Peter urges “casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you” [S2]. Together they point to taking one day at a time and entrusting worries to God, who cares. Other passages may also address worry, but these are the ones supplied.

sources.text: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
Therefore “If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so, you will heap coals of fire on his head.”

inputs.question: What does the Bible teach about how to treat enemies?

answer: Jesus teaches, “love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you” [S1]. Paul gives practical examples: “If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink” [S2]. Both passages call for active good toward enemies rather than retaliation [S1][S2].

Jeremiah 29 is a letter to the people of Judah taken into exile in Babylon. The promise of verse 11 follows the announcement that the exile would last seventy years (Jeremiah 29:10).

inputs.question: List a few verses about trusting God.

answer:
- Proverbs 3:5-6: “Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding” [S1].
- Isaiah 40:31: “those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength” [S2].
- Jeremiah 29:11: “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future” [S3]. The commentary notes this promise was first addressed to the exiles in Babylon, after the announcement that the exile would last seventy years [S4].

sources.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,

inputs.question: What does the Bible say about God’s word guiding us?

answer: Psalm 119 pictures God’s word as guidance for daily life: “Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path” [S1]. Second Timothy says “Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness” [S2]. The psalm stresses direction for each step [S1], while 2 Timothy lists the ways Scripture teaches and corrects [S2].
